extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff, and counsel involved in practitioner disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order approving a settlement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 resolving disciplinary charges against a registered patent practitioner, describing stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions (suspension, publication, administrative actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may act on practitioner discipline under these statutory and regulatory provisions; jurisdictional citation grounds the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Proposed Settlement of Disciplinary Matter Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.26' may be submitted to the Under Secretary/USPTO Director for approval; a Final Order may approve the Agreement and set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary matters may be resolved by consent settlement under § 11.26, which, when approved, becomes a Final Order reflecting the parties' stipulations and agreed sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: California MCLE compliance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to remain an active member of the California bar, Respondent was required to complete a minimum of 25 hours of mandatory continuing legal education ('MCLE') during the period of February 1, 2009, through January 31, 2012 (the 'compliance period').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners admitted to the California bar and maintaining active status must meet the stated MCLE hours for the compliance period; failure to do so can lead to professional discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to maintain correct bar status to modify MCLE obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent believed in good faith he was required to meet only a proportional MCLE requirement of 9 hours because he had not practiced law for part of the compliance period; however, because Respondent did not enroll himself as 'inactive' with the California bar, he remained obligated to complete the full 25 hours of MCLE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's obligation to complete reduced/proportional MCLE depends on properly changing bar enrollment status; failure to timely enroll as inactive does not reduce MCLE obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to report MCLE compliance accurately to the State Bar
rubrics_metrics.description: When Respondent reported to the California bar that he was in compliance, he knew he had only completed 9 hours of MCLE within the compliance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowingly reporting compliance when not met constitutes misconduct; accurate reporting to licensing authorities is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentation/act involving moral turpitude (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 6106)
rubrics_metrics.description: The California bar found that, by reporting to the State Bar that Respondent was in compliance with the MCLE requirements when he knew he was not, Respondent 'committed an act involving moral turpitude, dishonesty or corruption in wilful violation of Business and Professions Code, section 6106.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False statements to the bar about compliance may be characterized as moral turpitude under California law and support suspension or other discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO ethical violation triggering discipline — 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) by being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by the State Bar Court of California on or about September 25, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public discipline by a state bar on ethical grounds is a basis for USPTO disciplinary action under § 11.804(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension from practice before the USPTO (sanction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be, and hereby is, suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for thirty (30) days commencing on the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO may impose suspensions of specified duration as a sanction for violations; the scope can include patent, trademark, and other matters before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative effects of suspension — dissociation and PKI
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and Public Key Infrastructure ('PKI') certificates; Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number or a PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension includes disabling electronic access/credentials and preventing reissuance until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director publication and compliance obligations (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room, which is publicly accessible through the Office's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED must follow publication rules (including FOIA Reading Room posting) when issuing disciplinary Final Orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice content and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the specified text describing the practitioner's name, registration number, suspension duration, the ground (violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), dates of suspension and reinstatement, and that the action resulted from a settlement under the cited statutory/regulatory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official Gazette notices must communicate essential facts of the disciplinary action and the legal authority for the action; sample wording is provided in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Agreement or the Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order: (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning Respondent brought to the attention of the Office; (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent (i) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed, and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's settled disciplinary history may be used as aggravation or rebuttal in later complaints or proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement orders may specify that each party bears its own costs, rather than awarding costs to either side.
